messages:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a long-context bring-up on vectora-48k with int4-hybrid quant and started seeing a reproducible phase/offset shift when the request crosses ~32k tokens boundary. posting minimal repro and logs below.

alex: repro command i used: 
```
./run_infer --model=vectora-48k --quant=int4h --context=49152 --prefill=32768 --prompt-file=tests/longctx/anchor_chain.txt --seed=42 --max-new-tokens=1024
```

alex: observed: outputs diverge from fp16 baseline after ~+6 tokens past the prefill boundary; kv indices look sane but attention weights show a phase slip. not a memory OOM, more like index/rotation mismatch.

priya: can you paste a tiny log snippet from the runtime (kv indices + rotary phase)? that helped for earlier ropecache bugs. :mag:

alex: yes — relevant lines: 
```
[2025-11-03 09:12:14.123] KV_WRITE shard=3 seq_start=32768 seq_end=33792 idx_base=32768
[2025-11-03 09:12:14.124] ROTARY_APPLY layer=18 scale_factor=0.99987 pos=32795 phase=0.000123
[2025-11-03 09:12:14.124] ROTARY_APPLY layer=18 scale_factor=0.99987 pos=32796 phase=0.000130
[2025-11-03 09:12:14.241] ATTENTION_DOT layer=18 q_idx=1024 k_idx=32796 raw=0.0123 corrected=0.0119
[2025-11-03 09:12:15.512] OUTPUT_TOKEN token_id=5023 token_str="of" beam=0 prob=0.0012
```

alex: i instrumented a quick checksum over the kv slice and didn't see corruption: checksums before/after match. so likely a rotation/scaling mismatch across the modular boundary rather than a write corruption.

dmitri: interesting. do we see this only with int4h or also with int8/int16? can you repro with fp16 baseline and compare the rotary angles?

alex: good call — fp16 baseline is fine (no slip). int8-mid also fine. int4h shows the slip every time i cross >=32k prefill. tried swizzling batch sizes, same result.

priya: could be two things: 1) quantized kernel uses a slightly different pos_scale that accumulates error across the wrap; 2) compacted KV layout changes the q/k alignment when index > 32768 (shard boundary) and the rotary apply expects contiguous positions.

marie: can we quickly try an experiment toggling the rotary clamp/scale in the runtime? eg set pos_scale_clamp=0.125 and run the same prefill to see if amplitude reduces. also try forcing `rotary_mod = 65536` vs default.

alex: ran both. pos_scale_clamp=0.125 reduces the visible drift but doesn't eliminate the mismatch. forcing rotary_mod=65536 made the drift vanish on one run but flaked on repeated runs (non-deterministic).

dmitri: flakiness smells like an uninitialized accumulator or race in the kernel that only shows with reduced numeric headroom from int4h. was the kernel compiled with fma/fast-math changes?

alex: kernels compiled with -O3 same flags as int8. i did find one difference: the int4h packing path uses a tight memcpy path that aligns 64B chunks; when context crosses 32k the memcpy routine switches path (small remainder vs aligned). maybe boundary codepath is different.

priya: ah that could explain it — different codepath for tail copy leading to one-off shift on k indices. can you add an assertion in memcpy path to assert remaining_bytes == expected and log the branch taken?

alex: opened a quick PR on the runtime with extra logging and an assert in the tail copy. running suite now, ci-bot said the longctx smoke is queued.

ci-bot: [ci] queued tests: longctx/ropex_boundary_smoke, longctx/kv_integrity, quant/regression-harness. run id: 20251103-9842.

alex: run finished — kv_integrity passed, but ropex_boundary_smoke failed reproducing the slip. attaching new logs in the run.

marie: can you attach a minimal unit test that deterministically exercises the boundary branch? would prefer a small pytest that toggles packing_size and asserts no token divergence vs fp16 for first 64 tokens after boundary.

alex: yep i'll add test `tests/longctx/test_rotary_packing_boundary.py::test_int4h_tail_copy` with parametrized packing sizes. pushing now.

dmitri: also add a diagnostic that dumps rotary phases for a handful of layers (json) so we can diff int4h vs fp16 easily. even a CSV is fine.

priya: FYI i ran a quick eval with quant=fp16/8/4h and collected attention heatmaps — attaching screenshot to the PR. int4h shows a subtle phase shift at layers 16-20 right after the boundary.

marie: let's triage as: (A) add unit test + assert; (B) see if memcpy branch fix removes slip; (C) if persists, try deterministic kernel compile (no fast-math) and run hardware-level trace. priority medium. ping me if you need infra capacity. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks all — i'll post PR link and a short runbook for reproducing. keeping this thread as the canonical repo for notes.

ci-bot: [ci] new run posted: https://ci.internal.redwood/runs/20251103-9842/logs/ropex_boundary_smoke

alex: PR: https://git.internal.redwood/r/redwood/runtime/+/2345 — adds extra memcpy assert + diagnostic dump.

priya: ack, will review the test and heatmaps later today.

marie: nice work — if we fix this, it's probably worth adding to the onboarding checklist for any new long-context model (run the rotary packing boundary test).
